How Much of Dad's Day Do You Know Because He Told You?

Twelve quick questions about what the family knows of his routines and preferences. At the end: what you know, what's still unclear, and what to ask next.

Download PDF

Answer yes, no or not sure. This checks how much of your picture of Dad's day came from Dad himself. It doesn't measure Dad, and no answer here means he needs help or that anything should change.

  1. Has Dad told you, in his own words, what makes an ordinary day a good one?

  2. Do you know what Dad likes to be called by someone he's just met, because he has said so?

  3. Has he described to you how he likes his mornings and evenings to go?

  4. Do you know what he enjoys eating and when he usually has his meals, as he'd tell it today?

  5. For the foods he avoids, do you know which are simply his taste and which, if any, are an allergy or something a doctor told him?

  6. Has he told you which activities and which people he looks forward to in a week?

  7. Has he said how he likes people to talk with him and get in touch with him?

  8. Do you know, from him, what helps him feel comfortable somewhere unfamiliar?

  9. Is what you know written down, with a date and a note of who each thing came from?

  10. Has Dad read what was written, or had it read to him, and had the chance to change it?

  11. Has he said what he's happy to have shared, and with whom?

  12. Have you agreed with him how and when you'll ask again?

Answer the questions above and your page builds here.

        What this doesn't do

        It counts what Dad has told the family and what's been written down, not how Dad is doing, and not how well anyone knows him. A short “What you know” list means only that some things haven't been asked yet. Each one is an ordinary conversation, whenever it suits him.
